name: C2 — Mastery
description: Read novels, parse classical-flavored prose, debate philosophy, and switch register at will.

topics.title: Classical echoes (文言)
topics.description: The 之/其/所/而 family — and how they survive in modern formal writing

guide.intro: You will not be writing 文言 (wényán, classical Chinese) — almost no one does. But every Chinese newspaper editorial, legal document, government report, and serious novel is studded with classical particles, fossilized syntax, and four-character compressions that only make sense if you can read the classical underneath. Treat this as the X-ray vision unit.

sections.text: 之 (zhī) — the all-purpose connector

In modern colloquial Chinese 之 is replaced by 的. In formal writing 之 returns: it links a modifier to a noun (爱国之心 — "a heart of patriotism"), substitutes for an object pronoun (取而代之 — "take it and replace it"), and lurks inside dozens of 成语. Whenever you see 之 in a modern text, mentally swap in 的 or "it" and the sentence usually clicks.

rows.translation: What is said has reason — "that has merit."
To sum it up — used to open a closing paragraph.
A treasure of no price — priceless.

sections.text: 其 (qí) — "its / their / the said"

其 is the formal third-person possessive and a gentle determiner. In a contract you will read 其责任 (its/the responsibility). In an editorial: 其原因有三 (the reasons are three). Notice it never takes 的 after it.

rows.translation: In fact (lit. "its truth").
Each gets their proper place.
Among them / within it.

sections.text: 所 (suǒ) — turns a verb into "that which is V-ed"

所 + verb makes a passive-flavored relative clause: 所说 (that which is said), 所做 (that which is done), 所谓 (so-called). Pair it with 的 in modern usage to keep it readable: 我所说的话 — "the words I said." Reporters love this construction.

rows.translation: As is known to all — newspaper opener.
Unprecedented (lit. "never before existed").
The so-called experts — heavy with skepticism.

sections.text: 而 (ér) — "and / yet / and so"

而 fuses two predicates. Coordinative (年轻而有为 — young and capable), adversative (富而不骄 — rich yet not arrogant), or sequential (起而行之 — rise and act). Modern formal speech is full of it: spoken 而 sounds bookish; written 而 sounds polished.

Quick test: if you can replace 而 with English "and", "yet", or "thus" without losing the sense, you've parsed it. If none fit, you're probably looking at the fossilized 然而 (however) or 因而 (therefore).
Other classical fossils still alive

rows: 以…为… ("take X as Y"), 以便, 以免
若…则… ("if…then…"), 否则, 然则
几乎, 在乎, 不亦乐乎
记者, 学者, 读者, 强者
之乎者也 — the cliché of pedantry

sections.text: 之乎者也 (zhī hū zhě yě) is itself an idiom — it means "empty pedantic talk," mocking someone who hides behind classical jargon.

Don't conflate the two 也. Modern 也 is the high-frequency adverb "also / too" (我也去 — "I'm going too"). Classical 也 is a sentence-final marker that functioned roughly as a copula or assertion (… ， … 也 — "… is the case"). Same character, completely different jobs. In the table above, 也 is listed under its classical job; in everyday reading 99% of 也 you'll see is the modern adverb.
Literary number pairs

In literary or written-elevated register, paired numbers function adverbially to mean "a few / scattered." 一二 (yī èr) — "one or two," 三五 (sān wǔ) — "a handful," 七八 (qī bā) — "seven or eight, a small group." These appear in essays, captions, and novels — almost never in speech.

rows.source: 三五 好友 围炉 夜话。
rows.translation: A handful of close friends chatting around the stove at night.

rows.source: 一二 行人 匆匆 而 过。
rows.pinyin: Yī èr xíngrén cōngcōng ér guò.
rows.translation: A pedestrian or two hurrying past.

lessons.title: 之 in modern prose
lessons.description: Spot 之 inside fixed phrases and editorials

exercises.prompt: In a modern editorial, 之 most often functions like which colloquial particle?
exercises.explanation: 之 is the formal counterpart of 的 — it links a modifier to a noun in elevated register. The other particles (地 adverbial, 得 complement, 而 connector) handle distinct grammatical jobs.

exercises.prompt: the 之-idiom to its meaning
总而言之，通胀压力未减。
exercises.hint: An economics column ends with this — what is the writer signaling?
exercises.explanation: 总而言之 = "in conclusion / all in all" — a discourse marker for the wrap-up paragraph.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 之 in its classical-modern formal sense (modifier-linker)?
options: 他 走 之 后 我 才 来
国家 之 强盛 在 于 民
我 也 去 之
之 是 什么 意思
exercises.answer: 国家 之 强盛 在 于 民
exercises.explanation: 国家之强盛 ("the strength of the nation") uses 之 as the formal modifier-linker = 的. The other options misuse 之 — option 1 is a fixed adverbial (走之后 is colloquial 之后), the others ungrammatical.

exercises.prompt: Build a long formal sentence: "The development of artificial intelligence is the great trend of our age, and it is irreversible."
exercises.answer: 人工智能 之 发展 乃 时代 之 大势 不可 逆转

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a formal editorial line. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 言之有理，行之有效，方为治世之策
options: 言之有理，行之有效，方为治世之策
说得有道理，做得很有效，才是治理的好办法
言而有信，行而果断，是治世的关键
话说得对，事做得好，国家就能治理
exercises.answer: 言之有理，行之有效，方为治世之策
exercises.explanation: Three uses of 之 (modifier-linker) plus 方为 (literary 才是) and 之策 (formal -strategy). The other options paraphrase the same idea in modern colloquial or near-colloquial register.

exercises.prompt: each 之-construction to the modern 的-equivalent (or paraphrase)

pairs.right: 改革的困难 — the difficulty of reform
一天的功夫 — a single day's effort
国家的根本 — the root of the nation
切身的痛苦 — pain felt in the flesh

exercises.prompt: 非一日之功可解。
exercises.hint: An editorial uses this phrasing — what is the 非…可… pattern?
options: Classical negation pattern — "not something a day's effort can solve"
exercises.answer: Classical negation pattern — "not something a day's effort can solve"
exercises.explanation: 非 X 可 Y = literary "not X-able by Y" — a fossilized classical negation that survives in editorials. Modern colloquial would say "不是一天就能解决的."

exercises.prompt: An editorial closes: "扶贫攻坚，非 ___ 之 ___ 可 成." Fill the two-character pair (a single day's effort).
exercises.explanation: 非一日之功可成 — "cannot be done in a day's effort." A boilerplate editorial closer that quietly hedges expectations.
无价 (without price) + 之 (formal 的) + 宝 (treasure).

exercises.prompt: An editorial closes: "教育乃国___大计." Fill the formal modifier-linker (one character).
exercises.explanation: 国之大计 = the great strategy of the nation. 之 is the formal modifier-linker.

exercises.prompt: 取而代之
exercises.explanation: 之 stands for an antecedent object — "replace IT." 而 sequences the two verbs.

exercises.prompt: Build: "The rise of this generation is a great event of our age." (formal)
exercises.answer: 此 代 之 崛起 乃 时代 之 大事

exercises.prompt: each phrase to its discourse role
A formal speech opener is read. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 国之根本，在于民；民之所盼，乃政之所行
options: 国之根本，在于民；民之所盼，乃政之所行
国家的根本是人民，人民期盼什么，政府就做什么
国家最重要的是百姓，老百姓要什么，政府就给什么
对国家来说人民是根，他们的愿望就是政策
exercises.answer: 国之根本，在于民；民之所盼，乃政之所行
exercises.explanation: Four 之-linkers plus 乃 (formal copula) and 所 + verb construction — high literary register. Distractors paraphrase in colloquial.

exercises.prompt: A speech ends: "此乃人民___所望。" Fill the formal modifier-linker.
exercises.hint: 之 or 的 — pick the literary one.
exercises.explanation: 人民之所望 — "that which the people hope for." 之 + 所 + verb is a classical relative-clause builder still alive in speeches.

acceptableAnswers: pain that cuts to the skin
exercises.explanation: 切肤 (cutting the skin) + 之 (formal 的) + 痛 (pain). A literary set phrase still widely used.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 之 in the CLASSICAL pronoun sense (= him/it/them)?
options: 我 以 此 为 戒 以 警 之
exercises.answer: 我 以 此 为 戒 以 警 之
exercises.explanation: 警之 = "warn them." 之 here is the classical object pronoun (= him/her/it/them). The other three use 之 as a modifier-linker (= 的).

exercises.prompt: Build: "It is no easy task — not a thing a single day's effort can accomplish." (formal)
exercises.answer: 此 非 易 事 非 一日 之 功 可 成

lessons.title: 其 and 所 — formal relatives
lessons.description: The two particles that turn modern prose into a contract

exercises.prompt: 其原因有三
exercises.hint: What does this phrase most naturally mean?
exercises.explanation: 其 = "its/their"; 有三 = "are three (in number)." Classic essay-opener.

exercises.prompt: 所谓的专家
exercises.hint: Which tone does this phrase carry?
exercises.explanation: 所谓 = "so-called." Almost always loaded with doubt or sarcasm in modern usage.

exercises.prompt: the 所-phrase to its meaning

pairs.right: Naturally / as a matter of course

exercises.prompt: Build: "This is what we said." (formal)
exercises.answer: 这 是 我们 所 说 的

exercises.prompt: 其责任由甲方承担。
exercises.hint: In this contract sentence, what does 其 refer to?
options: The responsibility just defined in the prior clause
exercises.answer: The responsibility just defined in the prior clause
exercises.explanation: 其 = formal possessive/anaphor — "its responsibility" (i.e., the responsibility belonging to whatever was last named). Standard contract glue.

exercises.prompt: Build a contract clause: "The responsibility for it shall be borne by Party A; the costs shall also be paid by Party A."
exercises.answer: 其 责任 由 甲方 承担 其 费用 亦 由 甲方 支付

exercises.prompt: A reporter reads a sentence stuffed with 所 and 其. Pick the formal version.
exercises.spokenText: 众所周知，其影响之深远，前所未有
options: 众所周知，其影响之深远，前所未有
大家都知道，这影响很深远，从来没有过
据说，这事影响很大，是头一回
我们清楚，影响很大，史上第一次
exercises.answer: 众所周知，其影响之深远，前所未有
exercises.explanation: Two 所-constructions (众所周知, 前所未有), 其 + 之 chain. The distractors paraphrase in modern colloquial, official, or semi-formal registers.

exercises.prompt: A government white paper writes "___ 周知，气候变化已成全球共同挑战." Fill in the four-character all-knowing opener.
exercises.explanation: 众所周知 = "as is known to all" — the canonical 所-construction opener for editorials and policy papers.

exercises.prompt: each 其/所 phrase to its discourse function
Which sentence uses 所 INCORRECTLY for a C2 reader?
exercises.explanation: 所 + verb forms a noun-clause but only with transitive verbs taking an object that becomes the head — and 所吃饭 is ungrammatical because 吃饭 is already V+O. Correct would be 我所吃的饭. The other three are well-formed.

exercises.answer: the responsibility for it shall be borne by Party A
acceptableAnswers: the responsibility shall be borne by Party A
Party A shall bear the responsibility
responsibility for it is borne by Party A
exercises.explanation: 其 = formal anaphor ("its / their"); 由…承担 = formal passive "shall be borne by."

exercises.prompt: A policy paper begins: "___ 周知，气候问题已迫在眉睫." Fill the canonical four-character all-knowing opener.
exercises.explanation: 众所周知 = "as is known to all" — the textbook 所 opener for editorials.

exercises.prompt: 理所当然
exercises.hint: What does this set phrase assert?
options: It is self-evident / a matter of course
exercises.answer: It is self-evident / a matter of course
exercises.explanation: 理 (reason) + 所 + 当然 (naturally) — "as reason makes it natural." Used to assert a claim as obvious.

exercises.prompt: Build: "This is what the people hope for." (formal)
exercises.answer: 此 乃 人民 所 望

exercises.explanation: 前 (before) + 所 + 未有 (never had) — a classical four-character compression for "unprecedented."

exercises.prompt: A formal report opener is read aloud. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 众所周知，所谓的改革，其难度前所未有
options: 众所周知，所谓的改革，其难度前所未有
大家都知道，这种改革很难，从没见过
我们都明白，改革难度很大，史无前例
据说，改革的事情很复杂，难度不小
exercises.answer: 众所周知，所谓的改革，其难度前所未有
exercises.explanation: Three 所-phrases (众所周知, 所谓, 前所未有) plus 其 — stacked register markers. Distractors say similar things colloquially.

exercises.prompt: 无所谓
exercises.hint: Choose the closest reading in everyday use.
options: It doesn't matter / one is indifferent
exercises.answer: It doesn't matter / one is indifferent
exercises.explanation: 无 (none) + 所谓 (so-called / what is called) — literally "there is nothing to call it," so "it doesn't matter."

exercises.prompt: A contract clause: "___ 费用由乙方支付." Fill the formal anaphor (one character).
exercises.hint: The formal counterpart of 它的 / 这些.
exercises.explanation: 其 = formal possessive/anaphor — "its (i.e. the costs just mentioned)."

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 所 INCORRECTLY?
options: 我 所 说 的 话
前 所 未 有 的 事
众 所 周 知 的 道理
我 所 看 电影
exercises.answer: 我 所 看 电影
exercises.explanation: 所 + V forms a noun-clause head; 我所看的电影 (= the movie I watched) is correct, but 所看电影 with no 的 is ungrammatical.

exercises.prompt: Build: "What is so-called expertise is in truth only superficial knowledge."
exercises.answer: 所谓 的 专业 其 实 不过 是 皮毛

lessons.title: 而 — the bookish glue
lessons.description: And, yet, thus — depending on what flanks it

exercises.prompt: 富而不骄 (fù ér bù jiāo)
exercises.explanation: Adversative 而 — "X yet not Y." A standard literary praise pattern.

exercises.prompt: 年轻而有为
exercises.hint: Pick the most natural English translation.
exercises.explanation: Coordinative 而 — both qualities hold. 有为 (yǒu wéi) = "capable / promising."

exercises.prompt: Build: "He spoke briefly yet to the point."
exercises.answer: 他 说 得 简短 而 中肯

exercises.explanation: 然而 = literally "yet-and"; the workhorse contrastive in essays.

exercises.prompt: A literary-register sentence is read aloud. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 众所周知，前所未有之变局，非一日之功可解
options: 众所周知，前所未有之变局，非一日之功可解
大家都知道，这种没见过的局面，不是一天就能解决的
我们都明白，这是从来没有过的事情，需要时间
据报道，目前局势复杂，有关部门正在研究
exercises.answer: 众所周知，前所未有之变局，非一日之功可解
exercises.explanation: Classical fossils all stacked: 众所周知 (所), 前所未有 (所), 之 (formal of), 非…可解 (classical negation pattern). The other options say similar things in modern colloquial or official register.

exercises.prompt: 取而代之
exercises.hint: What is the role of 而 in this chengyu?
exercises.explanation: 取而代之 = "take, and replace it." The 而 here is the sequential connector — first 取, then 代之.

exercises.prompt: Build a literary-balanced sentence: "He is young yet steady; he speaks little but acts decisively."
exercises.answer: 他 年轻 而 沉稳 言 寡 而 行 果

exercises.prompt: the 而-phrase to its function (coordinative / adversative / sequential)

pairs.right: Fossilized discourse marker — to sum up

exercises.prompt: An essay reads: "政策推行 三年，___ 收效甚微." Fill the formal contrastive connector (one character).
exercises.explanation: 然 (or 然而) — formal "yet/however." The single-character 然 is the most literary; 然而 is essay-standard. 但 is more conversational.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence-final 也 is the CLASSICAL copula (not the modern "also")?
options: 他 也 不 知道
此 乃 国 之 大 事 也
你 也 来 了
exercises.answer: 此 乃 国 之 大 事 也
exercises.explanation: Classical 也 is sentence-final and assertion-like (≈ "is the case"). Pairs naturally with 此乃 ("this is") + 之 in literary register. The other three are modern adverbial 也 = "also/too."
然 (so / thus) + 而 (yet) — the workhorse essay contrastive.

exercises.prompt: An essay shift: "政策 推 行 三 年，___ 收效 甚微." Fill the formal contrastive (two characters).
exercises.explanation: 然而 — "however / yet." The literary turn. 然 alone is also acceptable in higher registers.

exercises.prompt: 富而不骄
exercises.explanation: Adversative 而 — "wealthy, yet not arrogant." A literary praise pattern.

exercises.prompt: Build (literary): "He is young yet steady; he speaks little yet his words have weight."
exercises.answer: 他 年轻 而 沉稳 言 少 而 有 分量

exercises.prompt: the 而-construction to its function
A literary-register sentence is read aloud. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 改革者，难而必行；改革之路，远而不可弃
options: 改革者，难而必行；改革之路，远而不可弃
改革这件事很难，但一定要做，路虽远不能放弃
改革很难做，但必须做，前路漫长不可丢弃
搞改革，难度大，但要坚持，路远也要走完
exercises.answer: 改革者，难而必行；改革之路，远而不可弃
exercises.explanation: Two adversative 而 + 之 + 者 — high literary register. Distractors paraphrase in modern Mandarin.

exercises.answer: rise up and act on it
exercises.explanation: 起 (rise) + 而 (sequential) + 行 (act) + 之 (it). Sequential 而 plus classical pronoun 之.

exercises.prompt: A line of praise: "敏 ___ 好 学，言 ___ 中 肯." Fill the literary coordinator (one character, twice).
exercises.explanation: 敏而好学 (sharp and fond of learning) — a Lúnyǔ allusion. 而 coordinates parallel praise.

exercises.prompt: Which 而 is the SEQUENTIAL one ("and then")?
options: 富 而 不 骄
取 而 代 之
总 而 言 之
exercises.answer: 取 而 代 之
exercises.explanation: 取而代之 = "take, and then replace it" — first take, then substitute. The others are coordinative, adversative, or fossilized discourse markers.

exercises.prompt: Build (formal contrast): "The policy may sound elegant, yet in practice it is hard to apply."
exercises.answer: 此 策 听 之 雅 然 而 行 之 难

lessons.title: 以、则、者 — the rest of the toolkit
lessons.description: Three more classical particles you'll trip over weekly

exercises.prompt: "以…为…" means:
options: Take X as / regard X as Y
exercises.answer: Take X as / regard X as Y
exercises.explanation: 以学生为本 = "take students as the foundation" — boilerplate education-policy phrasing. (The canonical example is 以人为本 — rén-běn — "put people first," the Hu-era policy slogan.)

exercises.prompt: Build: "Our company puts the customer first." (use 以…为…)
exercises.answer: 我们 公司 以 客户 为 本

exercises.prompt: "若…则…" is the formal counterpart of which everyday pattern?
exercises.explanation: Both are conditionals. 若…则… is the literary register; 要是…就… is colloquial.

exercises.prompt: the 者-noun to its meaning

acceptableAnswers: speaks pretentiously / hides behind pedantic jargon
exercises.explanation: All four are classical particles bundled together — a label for hollow learnedness.

exercises.prompt: the classical compression to its modern function (these still appear in editorials and legal documents)

pairs.right: Therefore / for this reason (= 因此, formal)
That being so / in that case (= 那么)
Why is that? (rhetorical question, = 为什么)
X's relation to Y / X compared to Y

exercises.prompt: 是以本院驳回原告之诉讼请求。
exercises.hint: In this legal-opinion sentence, what does 是以 function as?
exercises.explanation: 是以 = 因此 / 所以 in elevated register. Watch for it in court opinions, government white papers, and editorial conclusions.

exercises.prompt: Build a formal conditional: "If the policy goes through, then the people will benefit; if not, then losses will mount day by day."
exercises.answer: 政策 若 行 则 民 受 其 利 不 行 则 损 日 增

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a 文言-flavored editorial close. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 是以本部门决定，自即日起，相关政策依法施行
options: 是以本部门决定，自即日起，相关政策依法施行
因此我们部门决定，从今天开始，相关政策按法律执行
所以这个部门决定，从这天开始，要按规定办理
据此，部门已经决定，今天起就开始执行
exercises.answer: 是以本部门决定，自即日起，相关政策依法施行
exercises.explanation: 是以 (formal 因此), 本部门 (this department), 自即日起 (formal 从今天开始), 依法施行 (formal "executed in accordance with law") — four register markers. The distractors translate the same content into ordinary or near-formal Chinese.

exercises.prompt: Pair completion: "___ 你 已 决定，则 不必 再 犹豫." Fill the literary premise marker (two characters).
exercises.explanation: 既然…则… (literary) = 既然…就… (modern). Both halves carry the conclusion forward; 则 is the bookish counterpart of 就.

exercises.prompt: Which use of 以 is the CLASSICAL "in order to / so as to" (purpose)?
options: 他 以 学生 的 身份 发言
我 以 此 为 戒 以 免 重 蹈 覆辙
用 这个 方法 解决
我 以为 他 不来
exercises.answer: 我 以 此 为 戒 以 免 重 蹈 覆辙
exercises.explanation: The second 以 in 以免 ("so as to avoid") is the classical purpose marker — same root as 以便 ("so as to facilitate"). The first 以 here is 以…为… ("take… as…"); option 1 is identity-marking 以; option 4 is the verb 以为 ("think").

acceptableAnswers: regard the people as the foundation
take the people as the foundation
exercises.explanation: 以…为… — "take X as Y." Famous policy slogan.

exercises.prompt: A legal opinion closes: "___ 以 本 院 驳 回 原 告 之 诉." Fill the formal demonstrative (one character).
exercises.explanation: 是以 = "therefore / for this reason" — fossil 是 + 以, found at the head of court opinions and white papers.

exercises.prompt: 若 政策 行 之 有 效，则 民 受 其 利。
exercises.hint: What is the function of 则 here?
exercises.explanation: 若…则… = literary "if…then…" Pair with colloquial 要是…就… for the everyday version.

exercises.prompt: Build: "This being so, then there is no need to hesitate further." (formal)
exercises.answer: 既然 如此 则 不必 再 犹豫

exercises.prompt: the 者-noun to a near-synonym
A legal-register sentence is read aloud. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 是以本院驳回原告之诉讼请求
options: 是以本院驳回原告之诉讼请求
因此法院不接受原告的诉求
所以这个法院拒绝了起诉人的请求
据此，本院不予支持原告主张
exercises.answer: 是以本院驳回原告之诉讼请求

topics.title: Tang poetry foundations
topics.description: 李白, 杜甫, 王维 — the lines every educated speaker can quote

guide.intro: Tang dynasty (618–907) poetry is the cultural reservoir Chinese speakers draw on the way English speakers reach for Shakespeare. You don't need to read every poem — but the half-dozen lines below are quoted in WeChat moments, business toasts, news headlines, and movie titles. Knowing them is the difference between hearing a language and hearing a culture.

sections.text: 李白 — the romantic

Lǐ Bái (701–762), nicknamed 诗仙 (the Poetry Immortal). Famous for moonlit drinking, untethered imagination, and homesickness. His 静夜思 (Quiet Night Thoughts) is the first poem Chinese children memorize.

rows.translation: Before my bed, bright moonlight —
I wondered if it were frost on the ground.
Lifting my head, I gazed at the bright moon —
Lowering it, I thought of my hometown.

sections.text: 故乡 (gù xiāng — hometown) is the most-loaded word in classical Chinese. It still freights modern songs, Lunar New Year speeches, and diaspora literature.

Textual note: the 床前明月光 wording above is the Ming-dynasty redaction (the version every Chinese child memorizes today). The earlier Tang variant reads 床前看月光 / 疑是地上霜 / 举头望山月 / 低头思故乡. If you ever see 看月光 / 望山月 in an academic citation, it isn't a typo — it's the older edition.
杜甫 — the conscience

Dù Fǔ (712–770), 诗圣 (the Poetry Sage). Where Lǐ Bái soars, Dù Fǔ documents — war, hunger, the displaced family. His phrase 国破山河在 ("the nation shattered, mountains and rivers remain") is quoted whenever a country loses something it cannot replace.

rows.translation: The state is broken; the mountains and rivers remain.
Spring in the city — grass and trees grow thick.
Moved by the times, even flowers shed tears.

sections.text: 王维 — the painter-monk

Wáng Wéi (701–761) painted in words and wrote on silk. His couplets are nearly silent: a stream, a bell, a single bird. The phrase 诗中有画，画中有诗 ("poetry in his paintings, paintings in his poetry") was coined to describe him.

rows.translation: Empty mountain — no one in sight.
Only the echo of voices is heard.
Bright moon shines between the pines.

sections.text: 苏轼 — the Song-dynasty bonus

Sū Shì (1037–1101) is technically Song, not Tang, but you cannot graduate without him. His line 但愿人长久，千里共婵娟 ("may we live long and share the moon's beauty across a thousand li") is the standard Mid-Autumn Festival blessing — printed on mooncake boxes nationwide.

rows.translation: May people endure (live long).
And share, across a thousand li, the moon's beauty.

rows.pinyin: Bù shí Lú shān zhēn miàn mù
rows.translation: I cannot see Mount Lu's true face —

rows.pinyin: Zhǐ yuán shēn zài cǐ shān zhōng
rows.translation: Only because I myself am in the mountain.

sections.text: Su Shi's couplet shares a sensibility with the proverb 当局者迷 ("the one inside the game is confused") — but the proverb itself comes from 旧唐书 (the Old Book of Tang), not from 题西林壁. They are quoted side by side because they say the same thing from different angles.

topics.title: Rhetoric and argumentation
topics.description: Parallel structures, hedges, and the rhythm of formal Chinese

guide.intro: Mandarin formal writing has a rhythm. It loves parallel pairs, four-character cadences, and concessive hedges that English would handle with one comma. Internalizing these patterns is what separates the C1 essay ("correct") from the C2 essay ("this could be in 人民日报").

sections.text: Parallel pair: 一方面…另一方面…
"On one hand…on the other…" The skeleton of every balanced opinion piece. The two clauses should be the same length and grammatical shape — that's where Chinese rhetoric earns its style points.

rows.source: 一方面 我们要发展经济，另一方面 也要保护环境。
rows.pinyin: Yì fāngmiàn wǒmen yào fāzhǎn jīngjì, lìng yì fāngmiàn yě yào bǎohù huánjìng.
rows.translation: On one hand we must grow the economy; on the other, we must also protect the environment.

sections.text: Concessive: …也好，…也罢
"Whether X or Y — either way…" A literary, faintly resigned tone. You'll see it in op-eds and novelistic narration. The pair must mirror — same word class, similar length.

rows.source: 成功 也好，失败 也罢，过程 才 重要。
rows.pinyin: Chénggōng yě hǎo, shībài yě bà, guòchéng cái zhòngyào.
rows.translation: Success or failure — what matters is the process.

rows.source: 你 信 也好，不信 也罢，事实 就 在 那里。
rows.pinyin: Nǐ xìn yě hǎo, bú xìn yě bà, shìshí jiù zài nàlǐ.
rows.translation: Believe it or not, the facts are right there.

sections.text: Choice and preference: 与其…不如… / 宁可…也不…
Two paired patterns for ranking options. 与其 X 不如 Y — "rather than X, better Y." 宁可 X 也不 Y — "would rather X than Y." Both are written-register; both make the speaker sound deliberative.

rows.source: 与其 抱怨，不如 行动。
rows.translation: Rather than complain, take action.

rows.source: 他 宁可 辞职，也不 妥协。
rows.pinyin: Tā nìngkě cízhí, yě bù tuǒxié.
rows.translation: He would rather quit than compromise.

sections.text: Discourse shift: 倒是
倒是 (dào shì) — "on the contrary / actually / as it happens." A discourse marker that signals a gentle reversal of expectation. Not the dramatic 反而 — softer, more conversational-formal.

rows.source: 他 平时 话 不多，关键 时刻 倒是 很 果断。
rows.pinyin: Tā píngshí huà bù duō, guānjiàn shíkè dàoshì hěn guǒduàn.
rows.translation: He's usually quiet, but at critical moments he's actually very decisive.

rows.source: 你 这么 一 说，我 倒是 想起来 了。
rows.pinyin: Nǐ zhème yì shuō, wǒ dàoshì xiǎng qǐlái le.
rows.translation: Now that you mention it, I do remember.

sections.text: Building from a premise: 既然…就…
"Given that X, then Y." The premise is treated as agreed-upon — it shifts the conversation forward. Distinct from 因为…所以… (causal) and 如果…就… (hypothetical).

rows.source: 既然 你 已经 决定 了，就 别 再 犹豫。
rows.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ yǐjīng juédìng le, jiù bié zài yóuyù.
rows.translation: Since you've already decided, stop hesitating.

sections.text: Cause-and-effect chain: 之所以…是因为…
"The reason X is because Y." Stylistically inverted from English — Chinese leads with the consequence and only later names the cause. Beloved by editorialists building suspense.

rows.source: 他 之所以 成功，是 因为 他 从 不 放弃。
rows.pinyin: Tā zhī suǒyǐ chénggōng, shì yīnwèi tā cóng bù fàngqì.
rows.translation: The reason he succeeded is that he never gives up.

sections.text: Four-character rhythm rule: when in doubt, balance. 不仅…而且… is fine; 不仅 simple, 而且 ornate sounds wrong. Match the weight of the two clauses and your sentence will sound native.

lessons.title: Parallel pairs
lessons.description: 一方面 / 另一方面 and rhythmic balance

exercises.prompt: Build: "On one hand we must develop the economy, on the other we must protect the environment."
exercises.answer: 一方面 我们 要 发展 经济 另一方面 也 要 保护 环境

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has the most balanced rhetorical rhythm?
options: 一方面要兼顾效率，另一方面要切实地保障社会公平。
一方面要兼顾效率，另一方面要保障公平。
一方面要努力兼顾效率问题，另一方面要保障公平。
一方面要兼顾整体效率，另一方面要保障公平。
exercises.answer: 一方面要兼顾效率，另一方面要保障公平。
exercises.explanation: All four are grammatical; only the answer keeps both clauses at the same length and shape (要 + 2-char verb + 2-char abstract object). The others pad one side — "切实地保障社会公平," "努力兼顾效率问题," "兼顾整体效率" — breaking the parallel weight Chinese editorials chase.

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a parallel construction. Which of these has the cleanest balanced rhythm?
exercises.spokenText: 一方面要发展经济，另一方面要保护环境
options: 一方面要发展经济，另一方面要保护环境
一方面要发展经济，另一方面也要切实地保护好我们的生态环境
一方面经济，另一方面环境
一方面要发展，另一方面我们必须立即推进环境保护工作
exercises.answer: 一方面要发展经济，另一方面要保护环境
exercises.explanation: Both clauses: 要 + 2-char verb + 2-char object. Same syllable count, same shape. The padded options break the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Build a long balanced parallel: "On one hand we must heed people's hopes; on the other we must respond to people's worries."
exercises.answer: 一方面 我们 要 倾听 民意 另一方面 我们 要 回应 民忧

exercises.prompt: the parallel pattern to its essay function

pairs.right: Not only X but also Y — escalation
Either X or Y — listing alternatives

exercises.prompt: Which sentence shows the strongest 4-character cadence balance?
options: 我们要重视效率，同时也要顾及到公平问题
效率是重要的，公平也是重要的
我们应当兼顾效率和公平这两个方面
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses with parallel grammar (noun + verb + noun's role). Editorial cadence at its tightest. The other options say the same thing but lose the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Complete the balanced pair: "成功 ___ 失败 ___ 过程 才 重要." (Fill the two concessive markers.)
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罢 — "whether X or Y, either way…" Literary concessive pair. Both halves must be matched in length.

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a long compound sentence. Pick the version with the most balanced parallel rhythm.
exercises.spokenText: 教育之于个人，关乎前途；教育之于国家，关乎未来
options: 教育之于个人，关乎前途；教育之于国家，关乎未来
教育对个人来说是关于前途的事情；教育对国家来说则关乎未来
教育对个人有影响；教育对国家也很重要
教育之于个人关乎前途，对国家来说关乎未来这一重要议题
exercises.answer: 教育之于个人，关乎前途；教育之于国家，关乎未来
exercises.explanation: Two clauses, perfectly mirrored: 教育 之于 X，关乎 Y. Same length, same shape, classical 之于 as the connector. The distractors all break the symmetry.

exercises.prompt: Why does Chinese formal writing chase clause-length balance more aggressively than English?
options: Chinese has no other rhythm — it's impossible to write without it
Cultural-rhetorical convention rooted in classical 骈文 (parallel prose) — balanced rhythm signals seriousness and care
Editors enforce it via word counts
exercises.answer: Cultural-rhetorical convention rooted in classical 骈文 (parallel prose) — balanced rhythm signals seriousness and care
exercises.explanation: 骈文 (parallel prose) trained centuries of writers to value matched clauses. Modern editorial Chinese inherits the instinct: balanced rhythm = serious writer. Imbalanced clauses sound rushed even when grammatically fine.

exercises.answer: efficiency first, fairness at the root
acceptableAnswers: efficiency comes first, fairness is foundational
exercises.explanation: Four-character + four-character — the editorial signature rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Build the rhythm: "___ 方面 我们 要 倾听 民意，___ 方面 我们 要 回应 民忧." Fill the parallel openers.
exercises.explanation: 一方面…另一方面… is the two-sided framing pattern. Both halves must be matched in clause length.

exercises.prompt: Which line keeps the tightest 4+4 cadence?
options: 我们要兼顾经济发展和环境保护这两件大事
经济发展，环境保护，都很重要
我们既要发展也要保护
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character parallel clauses; identical verb-object grammar. Editorial rhythm at its most compressed.

exercises.prompt: Build a tight 4+4 parallel: "Develop the economy; protect the environment."
exercises.answer: 发展 经济 保护 环境

exercises.prompt: the cadence to the editorial effect
Which version has the strongest parallel rhythm?
options: 效率比较重要，公平也得照顾到
我们应该兼顾效率和公平
效率是先要的，公平要作为根本

exercises.source: 教育之于国家，关乎未来
exercises.answer: education, to a nation, concerns its future
acceptableAnswers: for a nation, education is its future
education matters to the nation's future
exercises.explanation: 之于 = formal "with respect to." The line mirrors a preceding one about 教育之于个人.

exercises.prompt: Mirror the editorial pair: "教育 之 于 个人，关乎 前途；教育 之 ___ 国家，关乎 未来." Fill the formal preposition (one character).
exercises.explanation: 之于 — literary "with respect to."

exercises.prompt: Which line below is the LEAST balanced for an editorial?
options: 我们应当兼顾整体效率，也要关心一下公平的问题
exercises.answer: 我们应当兼顾整体效率，也要关心一下公平的问题
exercises.explanation: Mismatched clause lengths and softeners (一下) break the editorial cadence.

exercises.prompt: Build a literary parallel pair: "Listen to the people's hopes; respond to the people's worries."
exercises.answer: 倾听 民意 回应 民忧

lessons.title: 也好 / 也罢 — concessive shrug
lessons.description: Either way, the point stands

exercises.prompt: 成功也好，失败也罢，过程才重要。
options: Success matters more than the process
Win or lose, what matters is the journey
Failure is the mother of success
Don't try and you can't fail
exercises.answer: Win or lose, what matters is the journey

exercises.prompt: Build: "Believe it or not, the facts are right there."
exercises.answer: 你 信 也好 不信 也罢 事实 就 在 那里

exercises.prompt: What register does …也好，…也罢 belong to?
exercises.explanation: It carries a slightly resigned, philosophical tone. You hear it in newspaper columns and literary fiction, rarely in casual chat.

exercises.prompt: the C2-register connector pattern to what it does

pairs.right: Whether X or Y, either way…
The reason X is that Y

exercises.prompt: Build a long concessive sentence: "Whether the policy is finally adopted or rejected, public discussion has already gone deep."
exercises.answer: 政策 通过 也好 否决 也罢 公共 讨论 已 走 向 深入

exercises.prompt: A columnist reads a literary concessive line. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 成功也好，失败也罢，过程才是真正的财富
options: 成功也好，失败也罢，过程才是真正的财富
成功或者失败都没关系，过程才重要
不管是成功还是失败，过程是关键
无论成功失败，过程是真财富
exercises.answer: 成功也好，失败也罢，过程才是真正的财富
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罢 + 才是 + multi-character noun phrase carries the literary register. The distractors paraphrase the same idea in everyday or semi-formal Chinese.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence misuses 也好…也罢?
options: 信也好，不信也罢，事实就在那里
成功也好，失败也罢，过程最重要
他来也好，没来也罢，会议照常
天气也好，所以我去散步
exercises.answer: 天气也好，所以我去散步
exercises.explanation: Here 也好 means "is fine" (modern adjective use), not the concessive pair. The pattern 也好…也罢 requires two contrasting alternatives — option 4 has only one and is using 也好 in a totally different sense.

exercises.prompt: An op-ed reads: "赞 ___ ，骂 ___ ，时间 终 会 给出 答案." Fill the two concessive markers.
exercises.explanation: 赞也好，骂也罢 — "praise or scold, either way…" Two 1-character verbs balanced perfectly under the concessive frame.

exercises.prompt: the concessive pattern to its register subtlety

pairs.right: Highly classical — "even if X, still Y"

exercises.prompt: 赢也好，输也罢，他都已经走得太远。
exercises.hint: In this novelistic line, what does the 也好…也罢 contribute?
options: A weary, fatalistic tone — outcome no longer matters
exercises.answer: A weary, fatalistic tone — outcome no longer matters
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罢 carries a faintly resigned quality that's perfect for a novelist signaling that a character has passed the point of caring about outcomes. That tonal coloring is what separates it from the neutral 无论…还是….
也好…也罢 — slightly weary, philosophical concessive pair.

exercises.prompt: Build the concessive pair: "赞 ___，骂 ___，时间 终 会 给出 答案." (Fill the two markers.)
exercises.explanation: 赞也好，骂也罢 — "praise or scold, either way…"

exercises.prompt: Which sentence misuses the concessive pair 也好…也罢?
options: 信也好，不信也罢，事实就在那里
他来也好，没来也罢，会议照常
天气也好，所以我去散步
成功也好，失败也罢，过程最重要
exercises.answer: 天气也好，所以我去散步
exercises.explanation: 也好 here is the modern adjective "is fine," not the concessive marker — and the pattern needs two balanced alternatives.

exercises.prompt: Build a literary concessive: "Whether praised or scolded, time will give the answer."
exercises.answer: 赞 也好 骂 也罢 时间 终 会 给出 答案

exercises.prompt: the concessive to its tonal coloring
A columnist reads a literary concessive. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 信也好，不信也罢，事实就在那里
options: 信也好，不信也罢，事实就在那里
你信不信，事实都在那儿
无论你信不信，事实摆在那里
不管你信不信，事实都摆着
exercises.answer: 信也好，不信也罢，事实就在那里

exercises.explanation: Used alone, 也罢 means "so be it"; in pairs (也好…也罢), it carries half the concessive frame.

exercises.prompt: Concessive line: "政策 通过 也好，否决 ___ ，公共 讨论 已 走 向 深入." (one character + 罢)
exercises.explanation: 通过也好，否决也罢 — "passed or rejected, either way…"

exercises.prompt: What kind of speaker most likely uses 也好…也罢?
options: A columnist or novelist signaling weary detachment
exercises.answer: A columnist or novelist signaling weary detachment
exercises.explanation: Its slightly resigned, philosophical coloring suits literary op-ed and novel-narrator prose.

exercises.prompt: Build (literary novelistic): "Whether he wins or loses, he has already gone too far."
exercises.answer: 赢 也好 输 也罢 他 都 已经 走 得 太 远

lessons.title: 之所以…是因为…
lessons.description: Lead with the consequence, end with the cause

exercises.prompt: Build: "The reason he succeeded is that he never gives up."
exercises.answer: 他 之所以 成功 是因为 他 从不 放弃

exercises.prompt: Why might a writer prefer 之所以…是因为… over 因为…所以…?
options: It foregrounds the result and makes the cause feel like a reveal
It is grammatically required after 但是
exercises.answer: It foregrounds the result and makes the cause feel like a reveal
exercises.explanation: Inverting the order is a rhetorical move — it lets the writer build small suspense before naming the cause.

exercises.prompt: "既然你已经决定了，___ 别再犹豫。" — fill the blank.
exercises.explanation: 既然…就… is the fixed pair. Both halves carry the conclusion forward.

exercises.prompt: Build a long causal-reveal sentence: "The reason this reform has succeeded is precisely that it places the people's livelihood first."
exercises.answer: 这 项 改革 之所以 成功 正是 因为 它 把 民生 放在 首位

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads an inverted causal sentence. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 他之所以坚持下来，是因为他从未忘记最初的承诺
options: 他之所以坚持下来，是因为他从未忘记最初的承诺
他坚持下来是因为他没忘记最初的承诺
因为他没忘记承诺，所以他坚持下来了
他从未忘记承诺，所以他坚持下来
exercises.answer: 他之所以坚持下来，是因为他从未忘记最初的承诺
exercises.explanation: 之所以…是因为… is the essay-style inversion (lead with consequence, reveal the cause). The other three express the same idea in 因为…所以… or modern colloquial frames.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 之所以 INCORRECTLY?
options: 他之所以成功，是因为坚持
她之所以离开，是因为身体原因
我之所以喜欢，是因为它很美
之所以下雨，今天不出门
exercises.answer: 之所以下雨，今天不出门
exercises.explanation: 之所以 must attach to a clause as the consequence ("the reason X is…"), and is then completed by 是因为 + cause. Option 4 misuses it as a stand-in for 因为. The other three are well-formed 之所以…是因为… inversions.

exercises.prompt: Complete the inversion: "中国 经济 之所以 能够 持续 增长，___ 改革开放 政策 的 推动." Fill the cause-marker (3 characters).
exercises.explanation: 之所以…是因为… is the fixed inverted pair. The cause clause (改革开放政策的推动) follows 是因为 as the rhetorical reveal.

exercises.prompt: the causal connector to its register
这家公司之所以失去市场，是因为它忘记了用户。
exercises.hint: What rhetorical effect does leading with 之所以 have?
options: It builds suspense — the failure is named first; the cause becomes the reveal
exercises.answer: It builds suspense — the failure is named first; the cause becomes the reveal
exercises.explanation: 因为…所以… presents cause then effect; 之所以…是因为… inverts to lead with effect. The inversion turns the cause into a punchline — exactly what columnists want for impact.

exercises.prompt: Build a premise sentence (既然…就…): "Since the people have given their trust, then we must repay them with effort."
exercises.answer: 既然 人民 给予 我们 信任 我们 就 应当 以 努力 回报
the reason X is that Y
acceptableAnswers: X is the case because Y
the reason for X is Y
exercises.explanation: Inverted causal: result first, cause as reveal.

exercises.prompt: Inversion: "中国 经济 ___ 能 持续 增长，是 因为 改革开放 的 推动." (3 characters)
exercises.explanation: 之所以 leads with the result; 是因为 follows with the cause.

exercises.prompt: Why might a writer choose 之所以…是因为… over 因为…所以…?
options: It foregrounds the result and turns the cause into a reveal
It is required after 但是
exercises.answer: It foregrounds the result and turns the cause into a reveal
exercises.explanation: Inverting cause and effect builds rhetorical suspense — perfect for editorials.

exercises.prompt: Build: "The reason he persisted is that he never forgot the original promise."
exercises.answer: 他 之所以 坚持 下来 是因为 他 从未 忘记 最初 的 承诺

exercises.prompt: the causal connector to its register
A speaker reads an inverted causal line. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 这项改革之所以成功，是因为它把民生放在首位
options: 这项改革之所以成功，是因为它把民生放在首位
改革成功的原因是把人民生活放第一
因为重视民生，改革就成功了
改革靠的是把民生放第一
exercises.answer: 这项改革之所以成功，是因为它把民生放在首位

exercises.explanation: 由于…故… is the most formal of the causal patterns — closest to classical.

exercises.prompt: Premise: "___ 你 已 决定，就 别 再 犹豫." Fill the literary premise marker (2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 既然…就… — "since X (premise), then Y."

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 之所以 INCORRECTLY?
options: 他 之所以 成功 是因为 坚持
她 之所以 离开 是因为 健康
之所以 下雨 今天 不 出门
我 之所以 喜欢 是因为 它 美
exercises.answer: 之所以 下雨 今天 不 出门
exercises.explanation: 之所以 must attach to a clause as the result; 是因为 introduces the cause. Used alone for 因为, it is wrong.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Since the people have given us their trust, we must repay them with effort."
exercises.answer: 既然 人民 给予 我们 信任 我们 就 应当 以 努力 回报

lessons.title: Choice, preference, and 倒是
lessons.description: 与其…不如, 宁可…也不, and the discourse marker 倒是

exercises.prompt: 与其抱怨，不如行动。
exercises.hint: What does the 与其…不如… structure express?
options: A preference: rather than X, better Y
exercises.answer: A preference: rather than X, better Y
exercises.explanation: 与其 (yǔqí) sets up the dispreferred option; 不如 (bùrú) names what's better. The whole pattern is a deliberative comparison.

exercises.prompt: 他宁可辞职，也不妥协。
exercises.hint: What does the 宁可…也不 pattern signal about the speaker?
options: Strongly prefers the first option, rejecting the second
exercises.answer: Strongly prefers the first option, rejecting the second
exercises.explanation: 宁可…也不 — "would rather X than Y." The first clause is what the speaker chooses; the second is what they refuse, even at cost.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Rather than complain, it's better to take action."
exercises.answer: 与其 抱怨 不如 行动

exercises.prompt: 他平时话不多，关键时刻倒是很果断。
exercises.hint: What does 倒是 contribute here?
options: It introduces a gentle reversal of expectation — "actually / on the contrary"
exercises.answer: It introduces a gentle reversal of expectation — "actually / on the contrary"
exercises.explanation: 倒是 (dàoshì) is a soft contrastive — softer than 反而, conversational-formal. It signals that despite what one might expect, the opposite is true.

exercises.prompt: "你这么一说，我 ___ 想起来了." Fill the discourse marker that means "actually / now that you mention it."
exercises.explanation: 倒是 (or just 倒) marks the gentle realization — your remark caused an unexpected memory.

exercises.prompt: Build a long deliberative sentence: "He would rather sacrifice short-term profit than betray the trust of his customers."
exercises.answer: 他 宁可 牺牲 短期 利益 也不 辜负 客户 的 信任

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions. Pick the one with the cleanest 与其…不如… cadence.
exercises.spokenText: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之
options: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之
与其在那里坐着空谈道理，不如起来就赶紧去行动
与其讨论，不如行动起来积极地解决问题
与其坐下来谈论各种道理，不如行动
exercises.answer: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses with mirrored grammar (verb 而 verb-object). Classical-flavored balance — the C2 essay closer. The padded distractors lose the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: the choice/preference pattern to its rhetorical use

pairs.right: Recommending the better of two options
Strong preference, refusing the alternative at cost

exercises.prompt: Which captures the difference between 倒是 and 反而 most accurately?
options: 倒是 is sharper than 反而
倒是 is softer / more conversational; 反而 is sharper, often signaling unexpected counter-result
反而 is colloquial and 倒是 is rude
exercises.answer: 倒是 is softer / more conversational; 反而 is sharper, often signaling unexpected counter-result
exercises.explanation: 倒是 is a gentle reversal ("actually / as it happens"); 反而 marks a stronger, often surprising counter-result. C2 readers feel the difference instantly.

exercises.prompt: Complete the proverb-style line: "___ 抱怨 命运 不公 ， ___ 改写 自己 的 故事." Fill the deliberative pair (2 + 2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 与其抱怨命运不公，不如改写自己的故事 — "rather than complain about an unfair fate, better to rewrite your own story." Classic motivational rhetoric in deliberative cadence.

exercises.answer: rather than complain, better to act
exercises.explanation: 与其…不如… — the deliberative comparison.

exercises.prompt: Deliberative: "___ 抱怨 命运 不公，___ 改写 自己 的 故事." Fill the pair (2 + 2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 与其抱怨…，不如改写… — motivational rhetoric.

exercises.prompt: 他 宁可 辞职，也不 妥协
options: He would rather resign than compromise
exercises.answer: He would rather resign than compromise
exercises.explanation: 宁可…也不 — strong preference, refusing the alternative at cost.

exercises.prompt: Build (literary): "Rather than sit and debate the way, better to rise and walk it."
exercises.answer: 与其 坐 而 论 道 不如 起 而 行 之

exercises.prompt: the choice/preference pattern to its use
A literary line is read. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之
options: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之
与其坐着讨论，不如起来行动
exercises.answer: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之

exercises.explanation: Soft contrastive — gentler than 反而.

exercises.prompt: Reversal: "你 这么 一 说，我 ___ 想 起来 了." Fill the soft contrastive (2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 倒是 — marks an unexpected memory or admission.

exercises.prompt: How does 倒是 differ from 反而?

lessons.title: Higher-tier 成语
lessons.description: Six idioms that mark you as a serious reader

exercises.prompt: the 成语 to its meaning
Your team raises 1% of what is needed for disaster relief. A reporter writes: "这点捐款无异于___。" Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 杯水车薪 = a cup of water on a burning cartload — the textbook idiom for hopelessly insufficient help.

exercises.prompt: An alumnus donates a building and says "我只是___罢了." What did they say?
exercises.explanation: 饮水思源 — "drink water, remember its source." The standard humble phrase for a former student giving back.

exercises.prompt: A junior researcher publishes a quiet paper that quietly changes the field. Years later, a colleague says "她那篇论文真是 ___ — 之前大家几乎都没听过她的名字." Fill the blank.
acceptableAnswers: 一鸣惊人 (yī míng jīng rén)
exercises.explanation: 一鸣惊人 — "one cry stuns everyone" — fits an unknown who astonishes. Standalone, without a near-synonym crowding it.

exercises.prompt: the higher-tier 成语 to its literal image

pairs.right: Crows and sparrows make no sound
A cup of water for a cartload of burning firewood

exercises.prompt: An editorial about a record-breaking heatwave opens with "今夏的高温实属___，气象台近百年来从未记录过同等数据." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 前所未有 — "unprecedented" — fits records that break the historical baseline. Standard editorial collocation.

exercises.prompt: A judge enters the courtroom and the gallery instantly falls silent. A reporter writes "全场顿时___." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 鸦雀无声 — even crows and sparrows are silent — is the textbook idiom for an instantly hushed crowd.

exercises.prompt: An award citation reads: "她获此殊荣，可谓 ___ — 多年的耕耘终于得到了应有的认可." Pick the idiom that says "the reputation is earned."
acceptableAnswers: 名副其实 (míng fù qí shí)
exercises.explanation: 名副其实 — name matches reality — the standard endorsement of an earned title or reputation.

exercises.prompt: A tech blog warns: "创业者一夜爆红的故事 ___，但持续输出价值才是真正的难题." Pick the idiom signaling "unprecedented and stunning."
exercises.explanation: 一鸣惊人 here describes the splashy debut. The follow-up clause then deflates it — classic editorial rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Which of these would feel WRONG in an op-ed about fundraising falling short?
options: 募集到的款项不过 杯水车薪
募集到的款项实属 鸦雀无声
对受灾群众而言，杯水车薪也聊胜于无
面对庞大的缺口，这点钱无异于杯水车薪
exercises.answer: 募集到的款项实属 鸦雀无声
exercises.explanation: 鸦雀无声 describes a silent crowd, not insufficient funds. A native reader would feel the misfit instantly. Distractor-spotting at C2 means recognizing the image inside each idiom.

exercises.answer: a cup of water on a burning cartload
exercises.explanation: 杯水 (a cup of water) + 车薪 (a cartload of burning firewood). The classic idiom of insufficiency.

exercises.prompt: An editorial closes: "对受灾群众而言，这点款项不过 ___." (4 characters) Fill the idiom of insufficiency.
exercises.explanation: 杯水车薪 — the standard editorial idiom for a grossly insufficient effort.

exercises.prompt: A famous unknown publishes a quiet but field-changing paper. The fitting idiom is:
exercises.explanation: 一鸣惊人 — "one cry stuns everyone." Fits an unknown who astonishes.

exercises.prompt: Build the editorial line: "Faced with such a huge gap, this sum is hardly more than a cup of water on a cartload of fire."
exercises.answer: 面对 庞大 的 缺口 这 点 钱 无 异 于 杯水车薪

exercises.prompt: the C2 idiom to a fitting context

exercises.answer: 今夏的高温实属前所未有

acceptableAnswers: remember where the water came from
exercises.explanation: The humble alumnus's idiom.

exercises.prompt: A judge enters and the gallery hushes: "全场 顿时 ___." (4 characters)
exercises.explanation: 鸦雀无声 — total silence in a crowd.

exercises.prompt: An award citation: "她获 此 殊荣，可谓 ___ —— 多年 耕耘 终 得 认可." Pick the right idiom.
exercises.explanation: 名副其实 — "the title is earned" — endorses an earned reputation.

lessons.title: 塞翁失马 and the long forms
lessons.description: Idioms whose punchline is implied

exercises.prompt: "塞翁失马" is short for "塞翁失马，焉知非福." The full meaning is:
options: Bad luck now may prove to be good fortune later
A horse lost is a horse gone
The wise farmer never loses anything
exercises.answer: Bad luck now may prove to be good fortune later

exercises.prompt: Your friend missed a flight that later had a maintenance scare. Best response:
options: 看来是塞翁失马 — talk about a blessing in disguise.
真是杯水车薪 — that hardly helps at all.
果然是名副其实 — the reputation is earned.
确实是鸦雀无声 — you can hear a pin drop.
exercises.answer: 看来是塞翁失马 — talk about a blessing in disguise.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Don't worry — this may turn out to be a blessing in disguise."
exercises.answer: 别 担心 这 或许 是 塞翁失马

exercises.prompt: the long-form idiom to the punchline that completes it
"百闻不如一见" is best paraphrased as:
options: Hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once
It is better to hear than to see
A hundred questions deserve one answer
exercises.answer: Hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once
exercises.explanation: The idiom is a stock argument for first-hand experience. Often quoted before someone visits a place they have only read about.

exercises.prompt: An interviewee says "我相信 三人行必有我师." The implied register is:
options: Confucian humility — there is always something to learn from others
A literal claim about three travelers
exercises.answer: Confucian humility — there is always something to learn from others
exercises.explanation: From 论语. Quoted to signal teachability without sounding self-deprecating.

exercises.prompt: After a startup pivot succeeds, the founder writes "当初被裁员，如今想来真是 ___ ， 焉知非福." Fill the missing four characters.
acceptableAnswers: 塞翁失马 (sài wēng shī mǎ)
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失马，焉知非福 — the long form. Setting the punchline behind the comma is a common rhetorical pattern.

exercises.prompt: Which scenario LEAST fits 塞翁失马?
options: A canceled flight that avoids a maintenance issue
A failed job application that pushes someone into a better field
A chronic illness that forces healthier habits
A long-planned promotion that arrives on schedule
exercises.answer: A long-planned promotion that arrives on schedule
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失马 requires an initial misfortune that turns out for the best. A smooth, on-time success is just success.

exercises.prompt: Build the long form: "Old man at the frontier loses his horse — how to know it isn't fortune?"
exercises.answer: 塞翁 失马 焉 知 非 福

exercises.prompt: A professor quotes "学而不思则罔". The point being made is:
options: Learning without reflection leaves you confused / lost
Thinking is more important than learning
Both learning and thinking are useless
exercises.answer: Learning without reflection leaves you confused / lost
exercises.explanation: The full Analects line: 学而不思则罔，思而不学则殆 — both halves needed. 罔 here is closer to "lost / muddled" than "empty."

exercises.answer: an old man's lost horse — who knows it isn't a blessing
acceptableAnswers: bad luck may yet prove fortunate
the old man at the frontier lost his horse — perhaps a blessing
exercises.explanation: The classical long form. The punchline 焉知非福 carries the meaning.

exercises.prompt: After a startup pivot saved by the layoff: "当 初 被 裁 员，如今 想来 真 是 ___ ， 焉 知 非 福." (4 characters)
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失马 — set up; 焉知非福 — punchline.

exercises.prompt: An interviewee says "三人行 必有 我师" — what register and what attitude?
options: Confucian humility — there's always something to learn
A literal claim about three travelers
exercises.answer: Confucian humility — there's always something to learn
exercises.explanation: From 论语. Quoted to signal teachability.

exercises.answer: 塞翁 失马 焉 知 非 福

A friend offers a long-form consolation. Pick what you hear.
options: 塞翁丢马，怎么知道不是好事
丢了马的老头，可能是福气

exercises.answer: hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once
acceptableAnswers: one look beats a hundred reports
exercises.explanation: The stock argument for first-hand experience.

exercises.prompt: Confucian classic: "学 而 不 思 则 ___." (one character)
exercises.explanation: 学而不思则罔 — learning without reflection leaves one lost.

lessons.title: 歇后语 — set-up and punchline
lessons.description: The two-part sayings every native speaker recognizes

exercises.prompt: the set-up to the punchline
我现在真是泥菩萨过江啊…
exercises.hint: A coworker says this — what do they mean?
options: I can't help you — I'm in trouble myself
exercises.answer: I can't help you — I'm in trouble myself
exercises.explanation: The implied 自身难保 — "can't even save myself." A polite way to refuse a favor.

exercises.prompt: You worked on a project for a year and the client cancels. A friend says "哎，真是竹篮打水…" What's implied?
options: All your effort came to nothing (一场空)
exercises.answer: All your effort came to nothing (一场空)

exercises.prompt: Project manager says: "这次大家就 ___, 各显神通吧!" Fill in the set-up.
exercises.explanation: 八仙过海，各显神通 — each team member should bring their own special skills.

exercises.prompt: the 歇后语 set-up to the implied meaning in plain Mandarin
"竹篮打水，一场空" — which English captures the rhythm best?
options: Drawing water with a bamboo basket — all for nothing
A basket of bamboo — empty in shape only
Pouring water into bamboo — the drink keeps coming
exercises.answer: Drawing water with a bamboo basket — all for nothing
exercises.explanation: The two-part structure: image (basket can't hold water) → moral (effort came to nothing). The translation has to keep both halves visible.

exercises.prompt: Two coworkers are stretched thin and a third asks for help. One whispers: "我现在真是 ___ 过江，自身难保啊." Fill in the blanks.
exercises.explanation: 泥菩萨过江，自身难保 — a clay Bodhisattva crossing a river can't even save itself. The standard polite refusal.

exercises.prompt: Which 歇后语 best fits this situation: a junior employee endures unfair blame at a meeting and can't push back without losing their job.
options: 哑巴吃黄连，有苦说不出
exercises.answer: 哑巴吃黄连，有苦说不出
exercises.explanation: Bitterness that can't be voiced — exactly the office-grievance scenario.

exercises.prompt: 歇后语 are most natural in which register?
options: Casual speech, online chat, family conversation
exercises.answer: Casual speech, online chat, family conversation
exercises.explanation: 歇后语 are colloquial — they bring warmth and humor. Avoid them in formal print; reach for 成语 instead.

exercises.explanation: 自身难保 — can't even save oneself.

options: Casual speech, online chat, family conversation

lessons.title: Suffering you can't voice
lessons.description: 哑巴吃黄连 and the idioms of swallowed pain

exercises.prompt: 我真是哑巴吃黄连…
exercises.hint: An employee who can't complain about an unfair boss says this — what does it mean?
options: I have bitterness I can't speak of
exercises.answer: I have bitterness I can't speak of
exercises.explanation: 黄连 is a bitter Chinese herb. Implied second half: 有苦说不出.

exercises.prompt: the saying to a situation it fits

pairs.right: Deal collapses after months of work
Refusing a favor when you're stretched thin
Team ad-libs — each plays their strength

exercises.prompt: Which is more likely in a formal newspaper editorial?
exercises.explanation: 成语 (four-character, classical) belong in editorials. 歇后语 are colloquial and rare in formal print.

exercises.prompt: 黄连 in 哑巴吃黄连 refers to:
exercises.explanation: 黄连 is one of the bitterest items in the traditional pharmacy. The image: someone unable to speak but with the worst taste in their mouth.

exercises.prompt: Complete the saying: "哑巴吃黄连，有 ___ 说不出."
exercises.explanation: 苦 here is doing double duty — literal bitterness (the herb) and metaphorical suffering (the unspoken grievance).

exercises.prompt: A novelist wants to describe a daughter-in-law trapped in an unfair household, suffering quietly for years. The most fitting phrase:
options: 她真是哑巴吃黄连，有苦说不出
exercises.answer: 她真是哑巴吃黄连，有苦说不出
exercises.explanation: Long suffering you can't voice — the textbook 哑巴吃黄连 scenario. The other idioms simply don't fit the shape of the situation.

exercises.prompt: An older relative complains "我这一辈子真是 哑巴吃黄连…" The implied next words and tone:
options: …百闻不如一见 — a fresh discovery
exercises.explanation: The trailing ellipsis after a 歇后语 set-up almost always invites the listener to mentally complete the punchline.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence most accurately uses 哑巴吃黄连?

topics.title: Confucian and Daoist concepts
topics.description: 仁、义、道、无为 — the philosophical vocabulary in modern usage

guide.intro: Modern Mandarin is haunted by two-and-a-half-thousand-year-old conversations. Words like 仁 (rén), 义 (yì), 道 (dào), and 无为 (wú wéi) appear in HR slogans, parenting books, and political speeches — usually drained of their original technical force, but never entirely. To read Chinese deeply you have to feel the philosophical residue.

sections.text: Confucian core: 仁 and 义

仁 (rén) is humaneness — the disposition to treat others as fully human. 义 (yì) is righteousness — doing the right thing even at cost. The compound 仁义 is shorthand for moral character. When a CEO is praised as 有仁义 (yǒu rén yì), they are being called principled, not merely successful.

rows.source: 他 是 一 个 仁义 之 人。
rows.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè rényì zhī rén.
rows.translation: He is a man of humaneness and integrity.

rows.source: 见 利 忘 义
rows.translation: See profit and forget righteousness — chase money and ditch principle.
Give up life to grasp righteousness — die for principle.

sections.text: 礼 — propriety, ritual, manners

礼 (lǐ) is the choreography of how relationships should be enacted — bowing depths, gift weights, who eats first. In modern business, 礼 survives as 礼貌 (politeness), 礼物 (gift), 送礼 (gift-giving), and the everyday verb 失礼 (to be rude / lose face by a breach of manners).

rows.source: 礼 多 人 不 怪
rows.translation: Excessive courtesy is never resented.

rows.source: 来 而 不 往 非 礼 也
rows.pinyin: Lái ér bù wǎng fēi lǐ yě
rows.translation: To receive and not give back is not 礼 — i.e. you must reciprocate.

sections.text: Daoist counterweight: 道 and 无为

道 (dào) is the underlying way of things — natural, ungraspable. 无为 (wú wéi) is "non-coercive action" — accomplishing through alignment rather than force. Modern usage has softened both: 道理 (reason, principle), 知道 (literally "know the way" — the everyday "to know"), 无为而治 (governing by stepping back).

rows.translation: Follow its natural course — let things be.
Govern by non-action — manage by enabling, not directing.
The highest good is like water — yielding, low-seeking, ultimately unstoppable.

sections.text: 上善若水 from the 道德经 is engraved on countless tea-shop walls and tech-CEO LinkedIn bios. Recognize it as Daoist signaling — humility-by-quotation.
中庸 — the middle way

中庸 (zhōng yōng), "the doctrine of the mean," prizes balance over extremes. In modern business and family advice, 中庸之道 (zhōng yōng zhī dào) is the polite phrase for "don't overdo it either way." Speakers reaching for it want to sound measured, even-keeled, philosophically grounded.

rows.source: 我 主张 走 中庸 之 道。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ zhǔzhāng zǒu zhōngyōng zhī dào.
rows.translation: I advocate the middle way.

sections.text: Be careful: 中庸 in younger urban use can be subtly negative — "wishy-washy, refuses to take a side." Read the speaker's tone.

topics.title: Regional language awareness
topics.description: Mainland Putonghua, Taiwan Guoyu, and the Cantonese world

guide.intro: "Chinese" is several languages and several standardizations of one. C2 means you can hear someone speak for ten seconds and tell whether they grew up in Beijing, Taipei, Guangzhou, or Singapore — and adjust your own usage accordingly. You won't speak every variant. You will learn to recognize and respect them.

sections.text: Putonghua vs Guoyu — same language, different standard

Mainland 普通话 (pǔtōnghuà) and Taiwan 国语 (guóyǔ) are the same language with different standardizations: simplified vs traditional characters, mainland Pinyin vs Taiwanese Zhuyin (注音), distinct vocabulary for many modern objects.
On the mainland 土豆 = potato. In Taiwan 土豆 = peanut. This single word has caused decades of dinner-party confusion.
Tone and accent cues

Mainland Putonghua, especially Beijing-flavored, has heavy 儿化音 (érhuàyīn, the rhotic suffix) — 哪儿、玩儿、有点儿. Taiwan Guoyu generally drops 儿化, prefers softer tones, and sounds the neutral tone less aggressively. Southern mainland speakers (Shanghai, Guangzhou) often blur the n/l distinction or merge zh/z, ch/c, sh/s.

rows.translation: Where are you? — Beijing-flavored.
Where are you? — Taiwan / southern / formal.

sections.text: Cantonese — a separate Chinese language

广东话 / 粤语 (Cantonese) is mutually unintelligible with Mandarin in speech, though written Standard Chinese is shared. Cantonese has six tones (some count nine), retains classical Chinese consonant clusters lost in Mandarin, and uses distinct vocabulary: 唔 (m̀h, not) for 不, 佢 (kéuih) for 他, 食 (sihk) for 吃.

sections.text: When you see characters like 嘅、咗、嗮、咩、嘢 in writing — that's written Cantonese (粤文), common on Hong Kong social media but unusual in mainland publications.
Singapore, Malaysia, overseas

Singaporean Mandarin (新加坡华语) is heavily code-mixed with English, Hokkien, and Malay. Vocabulary like 巴刹 (bāshā, market — from Malay pasar) and 德士 (déshì, taxi — from English) is locally standard but invisible on the mainland. Malaysian Chinese communities use similar mixes. Overseas Chinese in the US/Australia often retain pre-1949 vocabulary — 老中 for "older Chinese folks," or older transliterations.
Cross-strait political vocabulary — read the labels

Political register is where word choice tells you the speaker's stance. 大陆 (dàlù, "the mainland") and 内地 (nèidì, "the interior") describe the same territory but signal different framings — 内地 is the term Hong Kong and Macau use within the One-Country framework; Taiwan media usually prefer 中国大陆 or simply 中国. Likewise, 政府 (zhèngfǔ) is neutral "government," while 当局 (dāngjú, "the authorities") is more distanced — used by foreign-press translations and by speakers who want a faintly skeptical tone.

sections.text: These choices are not interchangeable. Calling Taiwan's elected government 台湾当局 ("the Taiwan authorities") rather than 台湾政府 is itself a political signal — standard in PRC official media. Reading register includes reading these tells.

topics.title: Media literacy and register
topics.description: Reading newspapers, recognizing propaganda, parsing satire

guide.intro: Reading Chinese news is not just decoding characters — it's reading register. The same event in 人民日报, 财新, BBC中文, 华尔街日报 中文版, and a 微博 satire account will appear in five distinct linguistic costumes. C2 means recognizing the costume.

sections.text: Boilerplate of the official register

Official Chinese reporting has a recognizable lexicon. When you see clusters of the phrases below, you are reading 党媒 (party media) or material that closely echoes it. They are not necessarily false — they are signals of register and stance.

rows: "The relevant authorities" — bureaucratic vagueness, agent unspecified
bù kě gào rén de mùdì
"Ulterior motives" — strong accusation of bad faith
"Hurt the feelings of the X people" — diplomatic outrage marker
"Seek progress while maintaining stability" — economic policy slogan

sections.text: "伤害中国人民的感情" is so formulaic that it has become a Chinese-internet joke. Recognizing the joke is part of recognizing the register.
Hedges of independent reporting

Independent or commercial Chinese-language reporting (财新, 端传媒, 联合早报, BBC中文) tends to use sourced hedges absent from official copy: 据悉, 据知情人士透露, 多名…表示, 截至发稿. These are signals of journalistic register.

rows.pinyin: jù zhī qíng rén shì tòu lù
rows.translation: According to sources familiar with the matter — Wall Street Journal cliché translated wholesale into Chinese.
At the time of publication — used to flag information that might change.
Has not yet responded — neutral phrasing for a no-comment situation.

sections.text: Satire and irony online

Chinese internet culture is famously inventive about evading censorship and signaling irony. Watch for: deliberate typos and homophones ("河蟹" hé xiè, "river crab", for the censored 和谐 héxié, "harmony"); reversed praise ("厉害了，我的国" — originally earnest, often deployed sarcastically now); the bracket-and-comma sneer like 「（笑）」 or 233333 (laughter); and the soft "emmm…" hedge marking polite disagreement.

rows.translation: "Awesome, my country" + "(laughs)" — sarcasm.

rows.pinyin: Zhè bō cāozuò wǒ gěi mǎn fēn
rows.translation: I give this move a perfect ten — almost always sarcastic praise of a misstep.
Those who understand, understand — wink, the censored thing.

sections.text: "懂的都懂" is a strong tell. The writer is naming the unspoken topic without naming it; you're being included in an in-group of readers.
Headline conventions

Chinese-language headlines compress aggressively. Expect colons, slashes, and bracketed labels: 【独家】 (exclusive), 【深度】 (deep dive), 【快讯】 (breaking). The colon often introduces the subject's quote: 张三：我没说过那句话.

topics.title: Formal essay structure (论说文)
topics.description: Openings, transitions, conclusions — the conventions of academic Chinese argument

guide.intro: 议论文 (yìlùnwén) — the argumentative essay — is the dominant academic genre in Chinese high schools, university entrance exams, and editorial pages. It has its own conventions: sourced openings, signposted transitions, weighty conclusions. C2 essay writing means writing inside this scaffold rather than translating English structure into Chinese words.

sections.text: The opening (开篇 kāipiān)

A 议论文 typically opens with one of three moves: a quoted line of classical or canonical authority (借古立论), an observation of a current phenomenon (现象切入), or a counter-position that the writer will then refute (破题). All three are register-marked — the colloquial "let me tell you about a friend of mine…" opener that works in English would feel out of place.

rows.source: 古人云："读万卷书，行万里路." 此言至今仍有 深意。
rows.pinyin: Gǔrén yún: dú wàn juàn shū, xíng wàn lǐ lù. Cǐ yán zhì jīn réng yǒu shēnyì.
rows.translation: The ancients said: "Read ten thousand books, walk ten thousand li." These words still carry deep meaning today.

rows.source: 近年来，人工智能 之 发展 日新月异。
rows.pinyin: Jìnnián lái, réngōng zhìnéng zhī fāzhǎn rìxīnyuèyì.
rows.translation: In recent years, the development of AI has changed by the day. (Phenomenon opener.)

sections.text: Transitions (过渡 guòdù)

Chinese academic writing signals its structure overtly. Each new paragraph typically begins with a connector that names its function: 首先 (first), 其次 (next), 再者 (furthermore), 此外 (besides this), 然而 (however), 反观 (looking conversely at), 综上所述 (summing up the above). Skip these and the essay reads as choppy, no matter how strong each paragraph is on its own.

rows: 首先 / 其次 / 再者
From this we can see — drawing inference
In sum / from all the above — pre-conclusion marker

sections.text: The body argument

Each body paragraph typically follows a 论点-论据-论证 structure: state a thesis-claim (论点), give evidence (论据), explain the reasoning (论证). The evidence is often a citation of a 名人 ("famous figure"), a historical episode, or a contemporary statistic. Hedges like 据统计, 研究表明, 不可否认 and 必须承认 mark the move from claim to evidence.

rows.source: 据统计，超过 七成 的 受访者 表示 …
rows.pinyin: Jù tǒngjì, chāoguò qī chéng de shòufǎngzhě biǎoshì…
rows.translation: Statistics show that over 70 percent of respondents say…

rows.source: 不可否认，问题 之 复杂 远 超 预期。
rows.pinyin: Bù kě fǒurèn, wèntí zhī fùzá yuǎn chāo yùqī.
rows.translation: It cannot be denied that the problem is far more complex than expected.

sections.text: The conclusion (结尾 jiéwěi)

The conclusion is rarely a meek English-style "in conclusion, …". A strong 议论文 ending circles back to the opening (照应开头), restates the thesis with elevated weight, and often closes with a four-character flourish or a forward-looking call. The phrases 综上所述, 由此可见, 总而言之 cue the reader to expect the wrap-up.

rows.source: 综上所述，唯有 持之以恒，方 能 致远。
rows.pinyin: Zōng shàng suǒ shù, wéi yǒu chí zhī yǐ héng, fāng néng zhì yuǎn.
rows.translation: In sum: only with perseverance can one reach far. ("方能" is the elevated form of 才能.)

sections.text: Convention #1 of academic Chinese: prefer the 4-character cadence in your closing line. 持之以恒, 方能致远, 任重道远, 砥砺前行 — these are not clichés, they are tonal closers that signal the essay is ending with weight.

lessons.description: 古人云, 现象切入, and the 破题 move

exercises.prompt: An essay opens with "古人云：\"读万卷书，行万里路.\"" This is which type of opening?
exercises.explanation: 古人云 / 古语有云 / 子曰 — all are signals that the writer is opening with a citation of canonical authority before staking their own thesis.

lessons.title: Transitions and signposting
lessons.description: 首先 / 其次 / 再者 / 反观 — making structure visible

exercises.prompt: the transition to its function
Halfway through an essay, a paragraph begins with "反观西方教育体系…". The writer is signaling:
options: A summary of what was just said
A pivot to a contrasting case used as comparison
exercises.answer: A pivot to a contrasting case used as comparison
exercises.explanation: 反观 = "by contrast / looking conversely at." A standard structural move in 议论文 — pivot to the comparison case to sharpen the thesis.

exercises.prompt: The pre-conclusion marker that means "summing up the above" is ___ (4 characters).
acceptableAnswers: 综上所述 (zōng shàng suǒ shù)
exercises.explanation: 综上所述 cues the reader: the wrap-up paragraph is starting. A near-mandatory move in formal Chinese essays.

exercises.prompt: An essay paragraph begins "不仅如此 ， 此 现象 在 农村 地区 尤为 明显." The 不仅如此 signals:
options: A new topic unrelated to the previous
exercises.explanation: 不仅如此 = "not only this" — a paragraph-level escalation that adds weight to the prior point. Standard essay rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Build a transition-rich sentence: "From this we can see that education reform must consider both efficiency and fairness."

exercises.prompt: the hedge to its move in the argument
An essay paragraph reads: "不可否认，问题之复杂远超预期。然而…". The 不可否认…然而… pair functions as:
options: Concession then pivot — "granted X, but Y"
A direct contradiction with no resolution
exercises.answer: Concession then pivot — "granted X, but Y"
exercises.explanation: 不可否认 lets you grant the opposing view's strongest point; 然而 then pivots to your counter-argument. Standard rhetorical move in formal argument.

topics.title: C2 review — register, idiom, classical, rhythm
topics.description: Mixed-register paragraph parsing, idiom-in-context, register identification, and parallel rewriting

guide.intro: C2 mastery is not knowing one register — it's switching between them in a paragraph and recognizing the switch when someone else does it. This review pulls together classical particles, 成语 in modern context, register identification, and the rhythm of parallel construction.

sections.text: What this review tests

Four lessons, each targeting one C2-level skill: (1) parsing paragraphs that mix classical particles with modern register; (2) identifying which 成语 fits a real headline / news context out of multiple plausible candidates; (3) reading a paragraph and naming its register (official, independent press, satire, literary, academic); (4) recognizing imbalanced parallel constructions and rewriting them so the rhythm holds.
If a question feels like it has two right answers, it usually does — at C2 the test is often "which is more idiomatic / more in-register," not "which is grammatical."

lessons.title: Mixed-register paragraph parsing
lessons.description: Classical particles in modern prose — read, then identify the function

exercises.prompt: A 财新 editorial reads: "众所周知，此次改革之于国民经济，影响深远。然而，其执行之难，前所未有。" Which classical particle is doing the most structural work?
options: 之 — modifier-linker (here connecting nouns into formal phrases)
exercises.answer: 之 — modifier-linker (here connecting nouns into formal phrases)
exercises.explanation: 之于 (relation to), 改革之… (this reform's…), 其执行之难 (the difficulty of its execution). Three uses of 之 carry the editorial register.

pairs.left: 此次改革之于国民经济
pairs.right: 之于 — X's relation to Y

exercises.prompt: A government report uses "是以本部门决定…". The 是以 is functioning as:
Build a mixed-register sentence: "The reasons are three; this we cannot ignore."

exercises.prompt: An editorial writes "此 乃 国 之 大 事 也." The sentence-final 也 functions as:
exercises.explanation: Sentence-final classical 也 was an assertion-marker in literary Chinese (≈ "… is the case"). Here it pairs with 此乃 + 之 to mark elevated register. The modern "also" 也 occupies a totally different syntactic slot.

exercises.prompt: Build a long mixed-register editorial sentence: "The development of artificial intelligence is the great trend of our time; it cannot be reversed, nor should it be feared."
exercises.answer: 人工智能 之 发展 乃 时代 之 大势 不可 逆转 亦 不必 畏惧

exercises.answer: 众所周知，此次改革之于国民经济，其影响之深远，前所未有
exercises.explanation: All four classical particles stacked: 众所周知 (所), 之于, 其, 之, 前所未有 (所). The other options paraphrase in modern colloquial or near-formal registers.

lessons.title: Which register is this?
lessons.description: Read the paragraph, name the register

exercises.prompt: "我方对此表示强烈不满，并已就此向有关方面提出严正交涉." Register?
exercises.explanation: 我方 + 表示强烈不满 + 有关方面 + 严正交涉 — four official-register markers in one sentence.

exercises.prompt: "据知情人士透露，截至发稿，公司方面尚无正式回应." Register?
exercises.explanation: 据知情人士透露 + 截至发稿 + 尚无回应 — the WSJ-style hedge cluster characteristic of 财新 / BBC中文 / 端传媒.

exercises.prompt: "这波操作我给满分，懂的都懂，233333." Register?
exercises.explanation: 这波操作 (sarcastic praise of a misstep) + 懂的都懂 (winking at censored topic) + 233333 (laughter). All three are unmistakable internet-satire markers.

exercises.prompt: "古人云读万卷书，行万里路。此言至今犹存深意。综上所述，唯有兼修，方能致远." Register?
exercises.explanation: 古人云 opener + 综上所述 pre-conclusion + 方能致远 4-character closer. All three are 议论文 conventions.

exercises.prompt: "空山不见人，但闻人语响. 返景入深林，复照青苔上." Register?
options: Tang-poetry literary register (王维 in fact)
exercises.answer: Tang-poetry literary register (王维 in fact)
exercises.explanation: Five-character per line, classical particles, painterly imagery — Tang poetic register. (This is 王维's 鹿柴.)

exercises.prompt: "研究表明，长期使用社交媒体与青少年焦虑水平显著相关." Register?
exercises.explanation: 研究表明 (citation hedge) + 显著相关 (statistical-correlation jargon) + 社交媒体与焦虑水平 (technical noun phrase). Three academic-register markers in one sentence.

exercises.prompt: "咱这事儿吧，说大不大说小不小，先放放看呗." Register?
exercises.explanation: 咱 (northern "we"), 事儿 (er-suffix), 说大不大说小不小 (colloquial reduplication), 放放看呗 (final particle 呗). Four colloquial markers — unmistakably casual northern speech.

exercises.prompt: "既然你已经决定了，那就放手去做吧。无论结果如何，我都支持你." Register?
exercises.explanation: 既然 + 那就 + 无论…如何… + 我都 — formal connectors, but the rhythm is conversational and the second-person address is direct. Sits between casual and literary.

exercises.prompt: "是以本院驳回原告之诉讼请求." Register?
exercises.explanation: 是以 (formal 因此), 本院 (this court), 驳回 (legal verb "dismiss"), 之 (formal modifier-linker), 诉讼请求 (legal NP "plaint request"). Five judicial-register markers.

lessons.title: Rhythm — fix the imbalanced parallel
lessons.description: Identify which clause breaks parallel weight, and rebuild it balanced

exercises.prompt: Which sentence keeps the cleanest parallel rhythm?
options: 一方面要兼顾效率，另一方面要保障公平。
一方面要努力地兼顾整体效率，另一方面要保障公平。
一方面要兼顾效率，另一方面要切实地保障好社会公平。
一方面要兼顾效率问题，另一方面要保障公平。
exercises.answer: 一方面要兼顾效率，另一方面要保障公平。
exercises.explanation: Both clauses are exactly 要 + 2-char verb + 2-char object. The other three pad one side and break the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Which is the imbalanced clause in this pair: "成功也好，失败这种事情其实也罢."
options: The first clause is too long
The second clause is padded — "这种事情其实" breaks the parallel with "成功"
exercises.answer: The second clause is padded — "这种事情其实" breaks the parallel with "成功"
exercises.explanation: 也好 / 也罢 demands matched short clauses. "成功 也好，失败 也罢" — two characters each side. Anything more is padding.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite the imbalanced sentence into balanced parallel form: "Believe it or not, the facts are right there."
exercises.answer: 你 信 也好 不信 也罢 事实 就 在 那里

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions of the same idea. Pick the one with the most balanced rhythm.
options: 与其在那里抱怨，不如赶紧采取一些行动
与其抱怨，不如积极地采取一些有效的行动
与其去抱怨这件事情，不如行动
exercises.explanation: Two characters versus two characters. The padded versions all break the cadence — that's the C2 rhythm test.

exercises.prompt: Which of these parallel constructions is most balanced?
options: 效率 优先 ， 公平 为 本
效率 是 我们 应该 优先 考虑 的 ， 公平 为 本
效率 优先 ， 公平 也是 一个 非常 重要 的 价值
我们 要 重视 效率 ， 同时 也 要 兼顾 公平
exercises.answer: 效率 优先 ， 公平 为 本
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses with parallel grammar (NP + V/role). The other three pad one or both sides and break the cadence.

exercises.prompt: Build a balanced parallel pair: "Education roots the individual; education shapes the country."
exercises.answer: 教育 立 人 教育 兴 国

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions. Pick the one in balanced classical-flavored cadence.
exercises.spokenText: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之
options: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之
与其坐着空谈各种道理，不如起来去采取行动
与其讨论，不如赶快行动起来
与其在那里讨论道理，不如行动
exercises.answer: 与其坐而论道，不如起而行之
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses, mirrored grammar (verb 而 verb-object). Classical-flavored 与其…不如… cadence at its most polished.

exercises.prompt: An editor flags this sentence as imbalanced: "我们应当倾听民意，回应民忧." The most likely fix is:
options: Match the first clause's structure: "我们应当倾听民意，我们应当回应民忧" (or both with 一方面 / 另一方面 framing)
exercises.answer: Match the first clause's structure: "我们应当倾听民意，我们应当回应民忧" (or both with 一方面 / 另一方面 framing)
exercises.explanation: Original: 我们应当倾听民意，回应民忧 — second clause drops 我们应当, breaking the parallel weight. The fix is to mirror the first clause's framing or use a parallel-pair connector. (Note: in some essay contexts the dropped second-clause subject is acceptable; the editor's call is style.)

exercises.prompt: Imbalanced: "成功也好，失败这种事情其实也罢，过程才重要." Fix the second clause to match: "成功 也好 ， ___ 也罢 ， 过程 才 重要." Fill with 2 characters.
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罢 demands matched two-character clauses. The original's "失败这种事情其实" is padding. The clean form is 成功也好，失败也罢.
